description: Evaluation cases for the canister-audit skill. Tests whether an agent, asked to audit an existing Rust ic-cdk canister, models invariants first, treats static hits as candidates (not verdicts), confirms the real flaw, and - the distinctive step - proves a confirmed HIGH/CRITICAL by reproducing the exploit in PocketIC, while handling unproven candidates and disclosure honestly.

output_evals.name: Audit an unguarded mint and move to prove it
expected_behaviors: Flags it: a state-changing update with no caller guard and no anonymous-principal rejection (pitfalls #2/#8)
States the anonymous principal can call it and mint a free balance, breaking an accounting invariant
Does not stop at the static observation - proposes PROVING it with a PocketIC reproduction (install the wasm, call claim_bonus as Principal::anonymous(), assert the balance/invariant)
Treats the grep/read hit as a candidate to confirm, not an automatic verdict

output_evals.name: High-recall static pass: candidate vs finding
output_evals.prompt: My static ruleset flagged `deposit`, `withdraw`, and `claim_bonus` as 'missing caller auth', but `deposit` starts with `if caller == Principal::anonymous() { trap }`. Is the ruleset wrong?
expected_behaviors: Explains the ruleset is deliberately high-recall and does not treat a bare == Principal::anonymous() as a suppressing guard
Says a flag is a candidate for review, not a confirmed finding
Concludes deposit's anonymous-rejection refutes its candidate, while claim_bonus (no guard at all) is the real finding to confirm and prove

output_evals.name: Write the PocketIC reproduction
output_evals.prompt: Write the PocketIC integration test that proves the token_vault `claim_bonus` flaw (an unguarded update that credits the caller's balance without touching total_deposited). Reply inline with just the Rust test file and the command to run it; don't create files.
expected_behaviors: Loads the built wasm32 canister into PocketIC (create_canister, add_cycles, install_canister)
Calls claim_bonus via update_call as Principal::anonymous(), then query_call for balance_of / total_deposited
Asserts the prohibited outcome (anonymous balance > total_deposited) so a passing test = a real exploit
Keeps the reproduction in a separate crate so the pocket-ic dev-dep does not touch the audited canister's manifest and the target is left unmodified

output_evals.name: Unproven candidate + responsible disclosure
output_evals.prompt: I think there's a TOCTOU across an await but I can't get a PocketIC test to trigger it. How do I report this, and this is an unpatched mainnet canister - can I publish the repro?
expected_behaviors: Says a clean/failed reproduction does NOT refute the finding - report it as suspected, not reproduced, keeping the reasoning
Does not downgrade a real-looking flaw to 'safe' just because the PoC did not trigger
Warns against publishing a working exploit for an unpatched canister; the repro goes in a private report to the controllers

output_evals.name: Discrimination: a guarded admin method is not a finding
expected_behaviors: Does NOT flag it as a confirmed finding: the guard attribute runs require_owner before the method, and require_owner rejects anonymous and non-owner callers
Treats the guarded admin method as passing on access control (may note it depends on OWNER being set correctly at init)

output_evals.name: Adversarial: guard called with its Result discarded
expected_behaviors: Flags admin_set_total as a real finding: require_owner() returns a Result that is discarded, so the mutation runs even when it returns Err
States any caller (including the anonymous principal) can set total_deposited
Recommends propagating the error (require_owner()?; with a Result return type) or using #[ic_cdk::update(guard = "require_owner")]
Does NOT accept the presence of the require_owner() call as a guard

output_evals.name: Adversarial: env-gated fetchRootKey is still a finding
output_evals.prompt: During the audit's static pass I found `if (process.env.DFX_NETWORK !== "ic") { await agent.fetchRootKey(); }` in the frontend. It only runs locally, so I can skip it, right?
expected_behaviors: Says NOT to skip it: it is a finding even behind an environment check
Explains fetchRootKey trusts the root key the replica returns, so if the branch reaches mainnet a man-in-the-middle can forge certified responses
Explains environment branching is how the call leaks into production builds
Recommends removing the call and passing the root key from the ic_env cookie (IC_ROOT_KEY) as rootKey to HttpAgent.create

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should load this skill vs. ones that should not.
should_trigger: Audit this Rust canister for security flaws
Review a canister I didn't write
Prove this canister exploit with PocketIC
Reproduce the vulnerability in my ic-cdk canister
Is this canister method actually exploitable?
should_not_trigger: How do I write a secure canister / what patterns should I follow?
How do I deploy my canister to mainnet?
Write a Candid interface for my canister
How do I launch an SNS?
